# Read-Side Patterns: Writing Query Handlers

:::info 镜像页
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 [`docs/guides/read-side-patterns.md`](https://github.com/idadawn/kun/blob/v2026.10.25/docs/guides/read-side-patterns.md)（`v2026.10.25`）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（[ADR-001 D1.8](/design/adr/adr-001-kun-relationship.md)）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见[与 Qian 的关系](/sdk/kun/with-qian.md)。改动请提到 kun 仓库。
:::

This guide covers the recommended patterns for query handlers in Kun. It assumes you understand
the write/read split; for the reasoning behind that split see
[docs/architecture/why-cqrs.md](/sdk/kun/architecture/why-cqrs.md).

***

## The Write/Read Rule

Query handlers must not use `KunDbContext`, `IUnitOfWork`, or any EF Core type. They connect to
the database via `IReadDbConnectionFactory`, run raw SQL with Dapper, and return flat DTOs. The
boundary is enforced by module dependencies: `Kun.Dapper` does not reference
`Kun.EntityFrameworkCore`, so adding an EF Core type to a query handler requires a deliberate
csproj change that reviewers will catch.

The short version:

- Command handler: inject `IRepository<T>` or `KunDbContext` (via EF). Transactional.
- Query handler: inject `IReadDbConnectionFactory`. No change tracking, no aggregates.

***

## Recommended Query Handler Pattern

The standard shape for a Kun query handler:

```csharp
using Dapper;
using Kun.Core.Cqrs;
using Kun.Dapper;

public sealed class GetProductByIdQueryHandler(IReadDbConnectionFactory connectionFactory)
    : IRequestHandler<GetProductByIdQuery, ProductDto?>
{
    public async ValueTask<ProductDto?> Handle(
        GetProductByIdQuery request,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        using var connection = await connectionFactory.OpenAsync(cancellationToken);

        const string sql = """
            SELECT id          AS "Id",
                   name        AS "Name",
                   description AS "Description",
                   price       AS "Price",
                   category_id AS "CategoryId",
                   stock       AS "Stock"
            FROM   catalog_products
            WHERE  id = @Id
              AND  is_deleted = false
            """;

        return await connection.QuerySingleOrDefaultAsync<ProductDto>(
            sql,
            new { request.Id });
    }
}
```

This is the actual handler from
`samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog/Application/Queries/GetProductByIdQueryHandler.cs`.

Key points:

- **`IReadDbConnectionFactory.OpenAsync`** returns an open `IDbConnection`. Wrap it in `using` —
  the factory opens a fresh connection per call and the caller is responsible for disposal.
- **Parameterized SQL** via the anonymous object `new { request.Id }`. Never interpolate values
  directly into the SQL string.
- **Column aliases** match the DTO property names exactly (case-sensitive on PostgreSQL). Use the
  `AS "PropertyName"` pattern consistently.
- **Soft-delete filter** (`is_deleted = false`) applied directly in SQL. There is no EF Core
  global filter on the read side — the SQL is the filter.
- The handler returns `null` when no row matches, which maps to a `404 Not Found` response via
  `Kun.AspNetCore`'s `Error.ToProblemDetails()` mapping.

***

## IReadDbConnectionFactory

`src/Kun.Dapper/IReadDbConnectionFactory.cs`:

```csharp
public interface IReadDbConnectionFactory
{
    Task<IDbConnection> OpenAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default);
}
```

The factory is a thin abstraction over a concrete ADO.NET provider. The sample implementation
using Npgsql (`samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog/Infrastructure/NpgsqlReadDbConnectionFactory.cs`):

```csharp
public sealed class NpgsqlReadDbConnectionFactory(ReadDbOptions options)
    : IReadDbConnectionFactory
{
    public async Task<IDbConnection> OpenAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        var connection = new NpgsqlConnection(options.ConnectionString);
        await connection.OpenAsync(cancellationToken);
        return connection;
    }
}
```

Register it in `Program.cs`:

```csharp
builder.Services.AddKunDapper(opts =>
    opts = new ReadDbOptions { ConnectionString = connectionString });

builder.Services.AddSingleton<IReadDbConnectionFactory, NpgsqlReadDbConnectionFactory>();
```

`AddKunDapper` is in `src/Kun.Dapper/DependencyInjection/KunDapperServiceCollectionExtensions.cs`.
It registers the `ReadDbOptions` singleton. Your `IReadDbConnectionFactory` implementation
receives it via constructor injection.

Note: `ReadDbOptions.ConnectionString` is `required init` — you must set it when constructing the
options object. The `AddKunDapper` overload shown above takes an `Action<ReadDbOptions>` callback;
set all required properties inside that callback.

***

## PageRequest and PagedResult

Use `PageRequest` and `PagedResult<T>` for paginated queries.

**`PageRequest`** (`src/Kun.Dapper/PageRequest.cs`):

```csharp
public sealed record PageRequest(int Page = 1, int PageSize = 20)
{
    public int Offset => (Page - 1) * PageSize;
}
```

- `Page` is 1-based.
- `Offset` computes the SQL `OFFSET` value automatically.

**`PagedResult<T>`** (`src/Kun.Dapper/PagedResult.cs`):

```csharp
public sealed class PagedResult<T>
{
    public IReadOnlyList<T> Items { get; init; } = [];
    public int TotalCount { get; init; }
    public required PageRequest Request { get; init; }

    public int TotalPages =>
        TotalCount == 0 ? 0 : (int)Math.Ceiling((double)TotalCount / Request.PageSize);
    public bool HasNextPage => Request.Page < TotalPages;
    public bool HasPreviousPage => Request.Page > 1;

    public static PagedResult<T> Empty(PageRequest request) =>
        new() { Request = request, TotalCount = 0 };
}
```

A paginated handler pattern:

```csharp
public sealed class ListProductsQueryHandler(IReadDbConnectionFactory connectionFactory)
    : IRequestHandler<ListProductsQuery, PagedResult<ProductDto>>
{
    public async ValueTask<PagedResult<ProductDto>> Handle(
        ListProductsQuery request,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        using var connection = await connectionFactory.OpenAsync(cancellationToken);

        const string countSql = """
            SELECT COUNT(*) FROM catalog_products WHERE is_deleted = false
            """;

        const string itemsSql = """
            SELECT id          AS "Id",
                   name        AS "Name",
                   price       AS "Price",
                   stock       AS "Stock"
            FROM   catalog_products
            WHERE  is_deleted = false
            ORDER  BY name
            LIMIT  @PageSize OFFSET @Offset
            """;

        var totalCount = await connection.ExecuteScalarAsync<int>(countSql);

        var items = await connection.QueryAsync<ProductDto>(
            itemsSql,
            new { request.Page.PageSize, request.Page.Offset });

        return new PagedResult<ProductDto>
        {
            Items      = items.ToArray(),
            TotalCount = totalCount,
            Request    = request.Page,
        };
    }
}
```

Run the count and items queries in the same open connection. Do not open two connections — use
Dapper's `QueryMultiple` if you prefer a single round-trip:

```csharp
const string sql = """
    SELECT COUNT(*) FROM catalog_products WHERE is_deleted = false;
    SELECT id AS "Id", name AS "Name", price AS "Price", stock AS "Stock"
    FROM   catalog_products
    WHERE  is_deleted = false
    ORDER  BY name
    LIMIT  @PageSize OFFSET @Offset;
    """;

using var multi = await connection.QueryMultipleAsync(
    sql,
    new { request.Page.PageSize, request.Page.Offset });

var totalCount = await multi.ReadFirstAsync<int>();
var items      = (await multi.ReadAsync<ProductDto>()).ToArray();
```

***

## DapperAotExtensions.QueryPageAsync

A `QueryPageAsync` extension that bundles the count + items dual-query into a single call is
planned (see TODO 2.3). Until it lands, use the patterns shown above directly.

***

## DTO Design

DTOs on the read side are intentionally flat. They are shaped for the API consumer, not for the
domain model.

Rules:

- **No aggregate nesting.** A `ProductDto` does not contain an `OrderDto`. If a view needs data
  from two aggregates, join the tables in SQL.
- **No domain types.** DTOs use primitive types (`string`, `decimal`, `Guid`, `int`) or simple
  value types. Never expose `Money`, `Address`, or other value objects from the domain layer in a
  DTO — that would create a dependency on `Kun.Core` in the read result.
- **Name for the consumer, not the table.** Column aliases can differ from table column names.
  Shape the DTO for what the API consumer needs to display or act on.
- **Immutable records.** Use `sealed record` with positional properties for DTOs. Records are
  value-comparable, serializable, and clearly signal "data container, not entity".

The `ProductDto` from the catalog sample:

```csharp
// samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog/Application/Queries/ProductDto.cs
public sealed record ProductDto(
    Guid Id,
    string Name,
    string Description,
    decimal Price,
    Guid CategoryId,
    int Stock);
```

The query from `GetProductByIdQuery`:

```csharp
// samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog/Application/Queries/GetProductByIdQuery.cs
public sealed record GetProductByIdQuery(Guid Id) : IQuery<ProductDto?>;
```

`IQuery<TResponse>` is a marker interface in `Kun.Core.Cqrs` that extends `IRequest<TResponse>`.
Using `IQuery` rather than `IRequest` directly signals intent and allows pipeline behaviors to
discriminate between commands and queries at registration time.

***

## Anti-Patterns

### Do not inject KunDbContext in a query handler

```csharp
// Wrong — do not do this
public sealed class GetProductByIdQueryHandler(CatalogDbContext db)
    : IRequestHandler<GetProductByIdQuery, ProductDto?>
{
    public async ValueTask<ProductDto?> Handle(...)
    {
        return await db.Products
            .Where(p => p.Id == request.Id)
            .Select(p => new ProductDto(...))
            .FirstOrDefaultAsync(cancellationToken);
    }
}
```

Problems with this pattern:

1. `CatalogDbContext` inherits `KunDbContext` which has global query filters, change tracking, and
   concurrency checks active. A query handler does not need any of this and pays the overhead.
2. `Kun.EntityFrameworkCore` is not AOT-candidate (`IsAotCandidate=false`). Injecting it into a
   query handler that runs in an AOT-published service will fail at publish time with trim warnings
   or at runtime with reflection errors.
3. `UnitOfWorkPipelineBehavior` calls `SaveChangesAsync` after every registered handler in the
   write pipeline. If a query handler is registered in the same pipeline stack as a command
   handler that has `UnitOfWorkPipelineBehavior`, the query will trigger a `SaveChangesAsync`
   call. This is harmless but wasteful — and it signals a pipeline configuration mistake.

### Do not load aggregates and project at runtime

```csharp
// Wrong — loads the entire aggregate graph, then discards most of it
var product = await _repository.GetByIdAsync(request.Id, ct);
return new ProductDto(product.Id, product.Name, ...);
```

Problems:

1. Loading an aggregate through `IRepository<T>` uses EF Core change tracking. Every property on
   the entity is loaded even if the DTO only needs three of them.
2. If the aggregate has navigation properties (owned entities, collections), EF Core may issue
   additional queries. The N+1 problem manifests here.
3. The aggregate is loaded into memory, partially read, then immediately discarded. The CPU and
   allocation cost is wasted.
4. Kills AOT compatibility for the same reasons as injecting `KunDbContext` directly.

Write the SQL to return only the columns you need. If the SQL feels verbose, that verbosity is
honest — it reflects exactly what data is fetched.

***

## AOT Note: \[DapperAot] Annotation

Dapper's classic `Query<T>` uses runtime reflection to build the object reader for `T`. In an
AOT-published binary, reflection is not available for types that were not preserved by the IL
linker, and the reader code is not generated.

The `[DapperAot]` attribute (from `Dapper.AOT`) instructs Dapper's source generator to emit the
reader code at compile time instead. The generated code is included in the binary at publish time
with zero reflection at runtime.

To use it, annotate the query method:

```csharp
using Dapper;

public sealed class GetProductByIdQueryHandler(IReadDbConnectionFactory connectionFactory)
    : IRequestHandler<GetProductByIdQuery, ProductDto?>
{
    [DapperAot]
    public async ValueTask<ProductDto?> Handle(
        GetProductByIdQuery request,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        using var connection = await connectionFactory.OpenAsync(cancellationToken);
        // ... SQL ...
        return await connection.QuerySingleOrDefaultAsync<ProductDto>(sql, new { request.Id });
    }
}
```

The Dapper AOT source generator scans for `[DapperAot]` and generates the reader for `ProductDto`
at build time. You will see the generated files under `obj/` after `dotnet build`.

If you forget `[DapperAot]` in an AOT-candidate project, the build will succeed but `dotnet
publish -p:PublishAot=true /warnaserror` will fail with a trim analysis warning indicating that
the reflection-based Dapper path is not trim-safe. This is the intended CI gate — the warning
catches missing annotations before deployment.

Ensure that the DTO record type is also AOT-visible. If the DTO is not referenced anywhere
statically (e.g. it is constructed only via Dapper reflection), add it to a
`[JsonSerializable(typeof(MyDto))]` context or reference it explicitly. In practice, returning the
DTO from a handler method counts as a static reference and the linker preserves it.

# SaaS 多租户策略选型指南

:::info 镜像页
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 [`docs/guides/saas-multitenancy.md`](https://github.com/idadawn/kun/blob/v2026.10.25/docs/guides/saas-multitenancy.md)（`v2026.10.25`）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（[ADR-001 D1.8](/design/adr/adr-001-kun-relationship.md)）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见[与 Qian 的关系](/sdk/kun/with-qian.md)。改动请提到 kun 仓库。
:::

> Kun Framework 通过 `Kun.Core.MultiTenancy` + `Kun.EntityFrameworkCore.MultiTenancy` 提供三种 SaaS 数据隔离策略：**Shared** / **SchemaPerTenant** / **DatabasePerTenant**。本文档帮你在合规、运维成本、租户规模三个维度上做出取舍，并给出各自的落地配方。
>
> 参考：[`docs/architecture/adr-p2d-multitenancy.md`](/sdk/kun/architecture/adr-p2d-multitenancy.md) · 白皮书 §12.2

***

## TL;DR 选型决策树

```
租户数 > 数百?
├─ 是 → 合规需要"单租户数据导出"?
│       ├─ 是 → SchemaPerTenant
│       └─ 否 → Shared
└─ 否 → 单租户数据量 > 数百 GB 或强合规（金融/医疗/GDPR 数据主权）?
        ├─ 是 → DatabasePerTenant
        └─ 否 → SchemaPerTenant（或 Shared 若对合规无硬要求）
```

## 对比表

| 维度 | **Shared**（共享库） | **SchemaPerTenant**（独立 Schema） | **DatabasePerTenant**（独立库） |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **隔离层级** | 应用层（`TenantId` 列 + 全局查询过滤器）+ PostgreSQL RLS 兜底 | 同库不同 schema | 完全独立的数据库实例 |
| **典型租户规模** | 数千到数十万 | 几百到几千 | 最多数百 |
| **单租户数据量** | 小（\< 几十 GB） | 中（几十 GB - 几百 GB） | 任意 |
| **合规友好度** | 普通 B2B SaaS | 支持"单租户导出"（pg_dump schema） | 强合规（数据主权、独立备份/RPO/RTO） |
| **运维成本** | 最低（单一数据库） | 中（schema 数量线性增长） | 高（数据库数量线性增长，secrets 管理） |
| **迁移执行时机** | App 启动时 `Database.MigrateAsync` | 租户开户时 `ITenantProvisioner.ProvisionAsync` | 租户开户时 `ITenantProvisioner.ProvisionAsync` |
| **实现基础件** | `AddKunTenantRls()` + `IMultiTenant` 全局过滤器（已落地 Sprint 1） | `AddKunMultiTenancy<T>(o => o.Strategy = SchemaPerTenant)` + `ITenantDbContextFactory<T>`（Part 2） | `AddKunMultiTenancy<T>(o => o.Strategy = DatabasePerTenant)` + `IDbConnectionResolver`（Part 3） |
| **跨租户查询** | 原生支持（`IgnoreQueryFilters`） | 不支持（需要单独的 `AdminDbContext` 枚举 schema） | 不支持（需要枚举所有连接） |

***

## 策略一：Shared

### 适用场景

- 租户数量大、单租户数据量小的 B2B SaaS（协作工具、CRM、业务仪表板）
- 合规要求普通（租户隔离满足"查询过滤 + defence-in-depth"即可）

### 落地配方

```csharp
// Program.cs
builder.Services.AddKunEntityFrameworkCore();
builder.Services.AddKunTenantRls();               // 启用 RLS 拦截器
builder.Services.AddDbContext<CatalogDbContext>((sp, opts) =>
{
    opts.UseNpgsql(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Default"));
    opts.AddInterceptors(sp.GetRequiredService<TenantRlsTransactionInterceptor>());
});
```

实体实现 `IMultiTenant`：

```csharp
public class Product : AggregateRoot<Guid>, IMultiTenant
{
    public string TenantId { get; private set; } = default!;
    public string Name { get; private set; } = default!;
    // ...
}
```

### 数据库侧 RLS 策略

```sql
-- 在 products 表上启用 RLS
ALTER TABLE products ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON products
    USING (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true));
```

`TenantRlsTransactionInterceptor` 会在每笔事务开始时执行 `set_config('app.current_tenant_id', @t, true)`，配合 PgBouncer transaction-pool 模式工作正常。

***

## 策略二：SchemaPerTenant

### 适用场景

- 租户数适中、需要"单租户逻辑导出"（`pg_dump -n <tenant>`）
- 每个租户共享同一 Postgres 实例但 schema 级隔离（兼顾合规与运维成本）

### 落地配方

```csharp
// 1. 注册策略 + 消费者自己的 ITenantDbContextFactory
builder.Services.AddKunMultiTenancy<CatalogDbContext>(o =>
{
    o.Strategy = TenantIsolationStrategy.SchemaPerTenant;
});

builder.Services.AddSingleton<ITenantDbContextFactory<CatalogDbContext>, CatalogTenantDbContextFactory>();

// 2. DbContext 在 OnConfiguring 读取当前租户，按 tenant_id 切 schema
builder.Services.AddDbContext<CatalogDbContext>((sp, opts) =>
{
    var tenantId = sp.GetRequiredService<ITenantContext>().TenantId ?? "public";
    opts.UseNpgsql(builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Default"))
        .UseKunSchema(tenantId)                          // 切 DefaultSchema + MigrationsHistoryTable
        .ReplaceService<IModelCacheKeyFactory, TenantAwareModelCacheKeyFactory>();
});

// 3. Consumer 自己实现 factory（~10 lines）
public sealed class CatalogTenantDbContextFactory : ITenantDbContextFactory<CatalogDbContext>
{
    private readonly string _connectionString;
    public CatalogTenantDbContextFactory(IConfiguration cfg) { _connectionString = cfg.GetConnectionString("Default")!; }
    public CatalogDbContext CreateForTenant(string tenantId)
    {
        var opts = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<CatalogDbContext>()
            .UseNpgsql(_connectionString).UseKunSchema(tenantId).Options;
        return new CatalogDbContext(opts, new FixedTenantContext(tenantId));
    }
}

// 4. 租户开户时调 provisioner
await provisioner.ProvisionAsync(new TenantInfo("tenant-acme"));   // 自动 CREATE SCHEMA + migrations
```

`TenantAwareModelCacheKeyFactory` 确保每个租户有独立的 EF 模型缓存键（否则第一个租户的已编译模型会被第二个租户复用，schema 错位）。

### 运维注意

- 迁移无法在 app 启动时批量跑（可能还没注册所有租户），必须走 `ITenantProvisioner` 的开户钩子。
- Deprovision 默认抛 `NotSupportedException`；设 `AllowDestructiveDeprovision = true` 才会 `DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE`。

***

## 策略三：DatabasePerTenant

### 适用场景

- 强合规（金融、医疗、GDPR 数据主权 = 不同租户数据不同地理分区）
- 单租户数据量大（单库 > 500 GB），需要独立备份/复制/RPO/RTO
- 租户数量较少（运维成本与租户数线性相关）

### 落地配方

```csharp
// 1. 注册策略（默认 resolver 从 TenantsConnectionOptions 读）
builder.Services.Configure<TenantsConnectionOptions>(
    builder.Configuration.GetSection(TenantsConnectionOptions.SectionName));
builder.Services.AddKunMultiTenancy<CatalogDbContext>(o =>
{
    o.Strategy = TenantIsolationStrategy.DatabasePerTenant;
});

// 2. Consumer factory 按 tenant 解析连接字符串
public sealed class CatalogTenantDbContextFactory : ITenantDbContextFactory<CatalogDbContext>
{
    private readonly IDbConnectionResolver _resolver;
    public CatalogTenantDbContextFactory(IDbConnectionResolver resolver) { _resolver = resolver; }
    public CatalogDbContext CreateForTenant(string tenantId)
    {
        var opts = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<CatalogDbContext>()
            .UseNpgsql(_resolver.ResolveConnectionString(tenantId)).Options;
        return new CatalogDbContext(opts, new FixedTenantContext(tenantId));
    }
}
```

appsettings.json：

```json
{
  "Kun": {
    "MultiTenancy": {
      "Tenants": {
        "ConnectionStrings": {
          "tenant-acme":    "Host=db-acme;Database=catalog;Username=u;Password=p",
          "tenant-fabrikam":"Host=db-fabrikam;Database=catalog;Username=u;Password=p"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### 关键约束

- **数据库 _创建_ 不在框架责任范围**：`DatabasePerTenantProvisioner.ProvisionAsync` 假设数据库已由运维流水线（Terraform / K8s Operator / 云 API）创建好，只跑 `Database.MigrateAsync` 拉齐 schema。如需自动 `CREATE DATABASE`，继承 `DatabasePerTenantProvisioner<T>` 覆盖 `ProvisionAsync`。
- **`DeprovisionAsync` 默认 no-op**：删除租户数据库的决策需要运维流程（连接池、复制、备份），框架不越权。
- **跨租户查询反模式**：禁止在 Command handler 里遍历所有连接做聚合查询。如需租户级管理视图，单独建一个 `AdminDbContext` 显式枚举连接池，并用不同的 `ICurrentUser` 角色守卫。

***

## 共通设计原则

1. **三种策略不混用于同一 `DbContext` 类型**：选一种注册，不要运行时切换（`IOptionsMonitor` 的 Strategy 变化不会重新连线 DI）。
2. **`ITenantContext` 始终是 scoped**：HTTP/gRPC 请求里由 `Kun.Security` 的 `JwtTenantContext` 填充；后台任务里由消费者按需注入。
3. **迁移工具链**：`dotnet ef migrations add` 需要 design-time `ITenantContext`。本仓库的 sample 使用 `DesignTimeTenantContext` 返回 `"public"` 作为占位符，避免 design-time 挂空依赖。

***

## 相关代码

- `src/Kun.Core/MultiTenancy/` — `ITenantContext`、`TenantIsolationStrategy`、`TenantInfo`、`ITenantProvisioner`、`NullTenantProvisioner`
- `src/Kun.EntityFrameworkCore/MultiTenancy/` — 全部三种策略的运行时件（`KunMultiTenancyOptions`、`ITenantDbContextFactory<T>`、`TenantAwareModelCacheKeyFactory`、`SchemaPerTenantProvisioner<T>`、`DatabasePerTenantProvisioner<T>`、`IDbConnectionResolver`、`OptionsBasedTenantConnectionResolver`、`TenantsConnectionOptions`、`KunMultiTenancyServiceCollectionExtensions`）
- `src/Kun.EntityFrameworkCore/Interceptors/TenantRlsTransactionInterceptor.cs` — Shared 策略的 RLS defence-in-depth
- `docs/architecture/adr-p2d-multitenancy.md` — 设计取舍完整 ADR

# Schema-per-service with `KunDbContext`

:::info 镜像页
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 [`docs/schema-per-service.md`](https://github.com/idadawn/kun/blob/v2026.10.25/docs/schema-per-service.md)（`v2026.10.25`）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（[ADR-001 D1.8](/design/adr/adr-001-kun-relationship.md)）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见[与 Qian 的关系](/sdk/kun/with-qian.md)。改动请提到 kun 仓库。
:::

> **Scope**: how to run multiple Kun-based services against a single PostgreSQL
> instance by giving each service its own schema (`catalog`, `order`, …), with
> business tables, the Outbox, Saga tables, and the EF migrations-history table
> all co-located under that schema.
>
> Applies to: any `KunDbContext`-derived DbContext using `Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL`.
>
> Last updated: 2026-04-22.

## Why schema-per-service

Running many services against one physical Postgres instance is operationally
cheap (one cluster to patch, one backup path, one connection pool). But putting
everything in `public` makes name collisions inevitable — two services both want
an `outbox_messages`, an `__ef_migrations_history`, and so on.

Kun's answer: each service overrides `KunDbContext.DefaultSchema` with its own
name (`"catalog"`, `"order"`, etc.), and `UseKunSchema(schema)` on the options
builder wires the migrations-history table into the same schema. A
`SchemaConsistencyInterceptor` then fails fast at the first `SaveChangesAsync`
if the two ever disagree, so misconfigurations surface in dev instead of
silently leaking rows across schemas in production.

## End-to-end recipe

### 1. Override `DefaultSchema` on your DbContext

```csharp
using Kun.Core.MultiTenancy;
using Kun.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

public sealed class CatalogDbContext : KunDbContext
{
    public DbSet<Product> Products => Set<Product>();

    public CatalogDbContext(
        DbContextOptions<CatalogDbContext> options,
        ITenantContext tenantContext)
        : base(options, tenantContext)
    {
    }

    /// <inheritdoc/>
    protected override string? DefaultSchema => "catalog";

    protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
    {
        base.OnModelCreating(modelBuilder); // applies HasDefaultSchema(DefaultSchema)
        modelBuilder.ApplyConfiguration(new ProductConfiguration());
    }
}
```

`KunDbContext.OnModelCreating` calls `modelBuilder.HasDefaultSchema(DefaultSchema)`
before applying the Outbox and tenant-filter configurations, so every
unqualified `.ToTable("x")` lands under `catalog`.

### 2. Chain `UseKunSchema("catalog")` in the design-time factory and DI

The design-time factory drives `dotnet ef migrations add`:

```csharp
using Kun.Core.MultiTenancy;
using Kun.EntityFrameworkCore.Extensions; // UseKunSchema lives here
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Design;

internal sealed class CatalogDesignTimeFactory
    : IDesignTimeDbContextFactory<CatalogDbContext>
{
    public CatalogDbContext CreateDbContext(string[] args)
    {
        var options = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<CatalogDbContext>()
            .UseNpgsql("Host=localhost;Database=catalog_design;Username=postgres;Password=postgres")
            .UseKunSchema("catalog")   // wires MigrationsHistoryTableSchema
            .Options;

        return new CatalogDbContext(options, NullTenantContext.Instance);
    }
}
```

Same pattern in the runtime `AddDbContext` call:

```csharp
services.AddDbContext<CatalogDbContext>((_, options) =>
    options
        .UseNpgsql(connectionString)
        .UseKunSchema("catalog"));
```

Order matters: `.UseNpgsql(...)` must precede `.UseKunSchema(...)` so the
relational provider extension already exists by the time `UseKunSchema` mutates
`MigrationsHistoryTableSchema`.

### 3. Regenerate migrations under the new schema

For an existing service already carrying `public`-schema migrations, regenerate
them once:

```bash
# Remove the old public-schema migrations
dotnet ef migrations remove \
  --project samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog \
  --startup-project samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog \
  --force

# Re-add under the new schema — the DesignTimeFactory's UseKunSchema("catalog")
# drives the correct MigrationsHistoryTable schema.
dotnet ef migrations add Initial_SchemaQualified \
  --project samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog \
  --startup-project samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog \
  --output-dir Infrastructure/Migrations
```

Inspect the generated `_Initial_SchemaQualified.cs` — every `CreateTable` /
`CreateIndex` / `DropTable` call now carries `schema: "catalog"`, and the
generated `ModelSnapshot.cs` starts with `.HasDefaultSchema("catalog")`.

#### Windows / Git Bash note

Both of the commands above must run with `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` in Git Bash,
otherwise `--project` values get path-mangled:

```bash
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 dotnet ef migrations add Initial_SchemaQualified \
  --project samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog \
  --startup-project samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog \
  --output-dir Infrastructure/Migrations
```

Run the two services' `dotnet ef migrations add` commands **sequentially**
(not in parallel) — they compete for the same `src/Kun.EntityFrameworkCore`
build artefacts.

### 4. Create the schemas in Postgres

`dotnet ef database update` will call `EnsureSchema("catalog")` via the
generated migration, so in most cases you do nothing. For a plain
`EnsureCreatedAsync()` flow (tests / quick prototyping), EF also issues
`CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS catalog`. You can create the schemas ahead of
time if you want the service accounts to have restricted grants:

```sql
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS catalog;
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS "order";  -- note: 'order' is reserved, quote it
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA catalog TO svc_catalog;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA "order" TO svc_order;
```

### 5. Verify with `dotnet ef migrations list`

After migrations regenerate, confirm the history table lives in the right
schema:

```bash
dotnet ef migrations list --project samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog
# shows catalog.__ef_migrations_history
dotnet ef migrations list --project samples/Kun.Sample.Order
# shows order.__ef_migrations_history
```

## The safety net: `SchemaConsistencyInterceptor`

`KunDbContext.OnConfiguring` unconditionally registers a
`SchemaConsistencyInterceptor` whose job is exactly one thing: compare
`Model.GetDefaultSchema()` against the relational provider's
`MigrationsHistoryTableSchema` at the first `SaveChangesAsync`, and throw
`InvalidOperationException` with a remediation hint when they diverge.

This catches the most common error — overriding `DefaultSchema` on your
DbContext but forgetting to call `UseKunSchema(...)` on the options builder.
Without the interceptor, business tables would land under `catalog` while
`__ef_migrations_history` silently stays in `public`, a migration-drift
timebomb. With the interceptor, the first save fails loudly:

```
InvalidOperationException: KunDbContext.DefaultSchema='catalog' does not match
MigrationsHistoryTable schema='(null)'. Call .UseKunSchema("catalog") on
DbContextOptionsBuilder to wire both consistently.
```

The check is gated by `Interlocked.CompareExchange` so it runs exactly once
per DbContext instance — zero overhead after the first transaction.

## Outbox and Saga co-location

Because the `KunDbContext` base class applies `HasDefaultSchema(DefaultSchema)`
**before** `ApplyConfiguration(new OutboxMessageConfiguration())`, the Outbox
table inherits the same schema without any extra configuration. Similarly,
Saga tables registered via `modelBuilder.ApplyKunSagaConfiguration()` land in
the service schema.

This is deliberate — having `catalog.outbox_messages` in the same schema as
`catalog.catalog_products` lets a single transaction atomically commit both,
which is the entire point of the Outbox pattern. Putting the outbox in a
shared `outbox` schema would break that atomicity story (cross-schema writes
still commit atomically, but the operational mental model gets muddier, and
separate grants / backup policies become harder to reason about).

## Running multiple services against one PostgreSQL

Once each service has its own schema, they can target the same physical
Postgres instance and the same logical database. Aspire wires this up
trivially — the `Kun.Sample.AppHost` sample points `Catalog` and `Order` at
the same `postgres` resource:

```csharp
var postgres = builder.AddPostgres("postgres");
var kun = postgres.AddDatabase("kun");

builder.AddProject<Projects.Kun_Sample_Catalog>("catalog")
    .WithReference(kun);
builder.AddProject<Projects.Kun_Sample_Order>("order")
    .WithReference(kun);
```

With schema-per-service in place, the two services coexist without name
collisions — each `SELECT * FROM catalog.outbox_messages` stays well-scoped.

## Reference implementation

- `src/Kun.EntityFrameworkCore/KunDbContext.cs` — `DefaultSchema` virtual
  property + auto-registration of the interceptor.
- `src/Kun.EntityFrameworkCore/Extensions/KunDbContextOptionsBuilderExtensions.cs` —
  the `UseKunSchema` extension.
- `src/Kun.EntityFrameworkCore/Interceptors/SchemaConsistencyInterceptor.cs` —
  the fail-fast guard.
- `samples/Kun.Sample.Catalog/Infrastructure/CatalogDbContext.cs` + migrations —
  concrete example with a `catalog` schema.
- `samples/Kun.Sample.Order/Infrastructure/OrderDbContext.cs` + migrations —
  concrete example with an `order` schema (plus Saga tables).
- `tests/Kun.IntegrationTests/Persistence/SchemaPerServiceTests.cs` —
  Testcontainers-backed test that boots two `KunDbContext` subclasses under
  distinct schemas against one Postgres and asserts physical isolation in
  `information_schema.tables`.

# Tracing Tour: Reading Distributed Traces in the Aspire Dashboard

:::info 镜像页
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 [`docs/observability/tracing-tour.md`](https://github.com/idadawn/kun/blob/v2026.10.25/docs/observability/tracing-tour.md)（`v2026.10.25`）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（[ADR-001 D1.8](/design/adr/adr-001-kun-relationship.md)）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见[与 Qian 的关系](/sdk/kun/with-qian.md)。改动请提到 kun 仓库。
:::

This document walks through the OpenTelemetry traces you will see when running the Kun sample
stack via `dotnet run --project samples/Kun.Sample.AppHost`. It assumes Docker and the Aspire
workload are installed and the stack is running. For setup instructions see
[docs/getting-started.md](/sdk/kun/getting-started.md).

***

## W3C Trace Context and OTLP

Every Kun service propagates traces using the
[W3C Trace Context](https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/) standard. Each in-process span records
a `traceparent` header that carries the `TraceId` and `SpanId`. When a request crosses a process
boundary — HTTP, gRPC, or the Outbox — the receiving side extracts the parent context and creates
a child span under the same `TraceId`. The result is a single trace tree that spans every hop
from the initial HTTP request to the final consumer acknowledgement.

Spans are exported via OTLP. When running under .NET Aspire the `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`
environment variable is set automatically to the Aspire Dashboard's collector endpoint. The
Dashboard collects and renders all spans without any additional configuration in the services
themselves. Framework modules (`src/Kun.*`) contain no OTel package dependencies — all
`AddKunObservability` wiring lives in the sample composition root
(`samples/Kun.Sample.Shared/OpenTelemetryExtensions.cs`) so the framework remains AOT-clean.

***

## What Instruments What

### Kun.Mediator

**ActivitySource name:** `Kun.Mediator`

`TracingBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>` wraps every `ISender.Send` and `IPublisher.Publish` call
(see `src/Kun.Mediator/Behaviors/TracingBehavior.cs`). It starts an `ActivityKind.Internal` span
named `Mediator.Send {RequestTypeName}` — for example `Mediator.Send CreateProductCommand` or
`Mediator.Send GetProductByIdQuery`.

The span is a child of the ambient activity at dispatch time, which is typically the ASP.NET Core
server span for the incoming HTTP request. Because the Mediator span is internal, it appears as a
nested block directly under the HTTP span in the Dashboard timeline.

Tags set on this span:

| Tag | Value |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| (none beyond span name) | The request type name is encoded in the span name |

If you want to add custom tags (e.g. command ID, tenant ID), do so from within the handler by
calling `Activity.Current?.SetTag(...)`.

### Kun.EventBus.Outbox

**ActivitySource name:** `Kun.EventBus.Outbox`

`OutboxPublisherBackgroundService` starts one `ActivityKind.Producer` span named `outbox.publish`
for each `OutboxMessage` it successfully publishes to the broker (see
`src/Kun.EventBus/Background/OutboxPublisherBackgroundService.cs`).

The critical detail is that the **parent context is restored from the stored row**, not from the
current ambient activity. When `EfUnitOfWork.SaveChangesAsync` writes an `OutboxMessage` row, the
`IntegrationEventOutboxAccumulator` captures `Activity.Current?.Id` and
`Activity.Current?.TraceStateString` and stores them in the `TraceParent` and `TraceState`
columns of the row. The background service reads those columns back hours or seconds later and
calls `ActivityContext.TryParse(message.TraceParent, message.TraceState, ...)` to reconstruct the
parent context before starting the publish span.

This means the `outbox.publish` span appears as a **child of the original producer span** in the
Dashboard, even though it runs in a different process tick, in a different background service
invocation, potentially seconds after the HTTP response was already sent to the client.

Tags set on `outbox.publish`:

| Tag | Value |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `messaging.system` | `outbox` |
| `messaging.destination` | Stable event type ID, e.g. `product.published.v1` |
| `messaging.message_id` | UUID of the `OutboxMessage` row |

### Kun.Grpc

**ActivitySource name:** `Kun.Grpc`

`KunTracingInterceptor` (see `src/Kun.Grpc/Interceptors/KunTracingInterceptor.cs`) runs first in
the interceptor chain registered by `AddKunGrpc`. It starts an `ActivityKind.Server` span named
`grpc.server` for each unary, client-streaming, server-streaming or duplex RPC call. The span
remains active until the awaited handler completes, including all stream operations.

Tags set:

| Tag | Value |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `rpc.system` | `grpc` |
| `rpc.method` | Full gRPC method path, e.g. `/catalog.CatalogService/GetProduct` |
| `rpc.type` | `unary`, `client_streaming`, `server_streaming` or `duplex_streaming` |
| `rpc.grpc.status_code` | Final gRPC status code; faults also mark the activity as Error |

If a downstream service calls a Kun gRPC service, the caller's `HttpClient` instruments propagate
the `traceparent` header via the standard gRPC client instrumentation wired in
`AddKunObservability`. The server interceptor picks up the parent context automatically from the
incoming metadata — `ActivityKind.Server` causes the OTel SDK to look for an inbound W3C header.

### Kun.Saga

**ActivitySource name:** `Kun.Saga`

`SagaStepExecutor` (see `src/Kun.Saga/Orchestration/SagaStepExecutor.cs`) starts one
`ActivityKind.Internal` span per step queue entry it processes. The span name encodes the
direction:

- `saga.step.execute` — forward execution of a step
- `saga.step.compensate` — reverse compensation of a step

Tags set:

| Tag | Value |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `saga.step_index` | Zero-based index of the step in the saga definition |
| `saga.saga_id` | UUID of the `SagaInstance` |
| `saga.direction` | `Execute` or `Compensate` |
| `saga.name` | Registered saga class name, e.g. `OrderCreationSaga` |

Note: these spans are started by the `SagaStepExecutor` background service polling loop. The
background service does **not** restore a producer trace context from the saga instance row — the
saga spans therefore appear as root spans or under whatever ambient activity the poll loop happens
to inherit. Cross-trace correlation via `saga.saga_id` is the intended mechanism; see the
[saga_id as cross-trace correlation](#sagaid-as-cross-trace-correlation) section below.

***

## How to Read a Happy-Path Trace

The happy path is triggered by `POST /demo/happy-path` against the Order service. This is what
you should see in the Aspire Dashboard Traces panel:

```
[HTTP POST /demo/happy-path]  ← ASP.NET Core server span (root)
  └─ [Mediator.Send PlaceOrderCommand]  ← TracingBehavior span
       └─ [outbox.publish order.completed.v1]  ← OutboxPublisherBackgroundService span
            (parent context restored from OutboxMessage.TraceParent)
```

The saga step spans appear separately because the `SagaStepExecutor` runs in a background
service:

```
[saga.step.execute]  saga.step_index=0, saga.name=OrderCreationSaga
[saga.step.execute]  saga.step_index=1, saga.name=OrderCreationSaga
[saga.step.execute]  saga.step_index=2, saga.name=OrderCreationSaga
[saga.step.execute]  saga.step_index=3, saga.name=OrderCreationSaga
```

To correlate these saga step spans with the originating HTTP request, use the `saga.saga_id` tag
(see the next section). Filter by the saga UUID in the Dashboard search bar to find all spans
associated with a single saga instance.

The timeline for the happy path looks like this in wall-clock order:

1. `POST /demo/happy-path` arrives. ASP.NET Core opens a server span.
2. `PlaceOrderCommand` is dispatched via `ISender.Send`. `TracingBehavior` opens a child span.
3. The command handler calls `ISagaOrchestrator.StartAsync`. This writes a `SagaInstance` row and
   the first `SagaStepQueueEntry` row inside the same EF Core `SaveChangesAsync` transaction.
4. The HTTP response is sent. The server span closes.
5. Seconds later, `SagaStepExecutor` polls `FetchPendingStepsAsync` and finds the queue entry.
   It opens a `saga.step.execute` span and runs `ReserveInventoryStep.ExecuteAsync`. On success,
   it enqueues step 1 and marks the entry processed.
6. Steps 1, 2, and 3 execute in sequence in subsequent poll cycles.
7. `NotifyCustomerStep` enqueues an `order.completed.v1` `OutboxMessage` row inside its
   `SaveChangesAsync` call. The `TraceParent` of the current `saga.step.execute` span is captured
   into the row.
8. `OutboxPublisherBackgroundService` polls, finds the pending message, restores the trace
   context from `TraceParent`, and opens an `outbox.publish` child span. The message is published
   to RabbitMQ and the row is marked `Published`.

In the Dashboard, the `outbox.publish` span correctly appears as a descendant of the saga step
that produced it, giving you the full causal chain in one view.

***

## How to Read a Compensation Trace

The compensation path is triggered by `POST /demo/trigger-payment-failure`. The trace structure
reflects the point of failure and the reverse execution:

```
[HTTP POST /demo/trigger-payment-failure]
  └─ [Mediator.Send PlaceOrderCommand]
```

Then in background poll cycles:

```
[saga.step.execute]  step_index=0  (ReserveInventoryStep — succeeds)
[saga.step.execute]  step_index=1  (ProcessPaymentStep — fails, span status=Error)
[saga.step.compensate]  step_index=1  (ProcessPaymentStep.CompensateAsync)
[saga.step.compensate]  step_index=0  (ReserveInventoryStep.CompensateAsync)
```

When `ProcessPaymentStep.ExecuteAsync` throws `SagaStepFailedException`, the executor:

1. Sets `activity?.SetStatus(ActivityStatusCode.Error, ex.Message)` on the failing span — visible
   as a red span in the Dashboard.
2. Transitions the `SagaInstance` to `SagaState.Compensating`.
3. Enqueues `Compensate` entries for steps 1 and 0 in reverse order.

The compensation spans appear with `saga.direction=Compensate` in their tags. Because they run in
the same background service with the same `ActivitySource`, they appear in the Dashboard's "all
spans" list alongside the execution spans. Searching by `saga.saga_id` brings them together.

To distinguish failure from normal completion in the Dashboard:

- A `saga.step.execute` span with `ActivityStatus=Error` is the failing step.
- Following `saga.step.compensate` spans at lower `step_index` values are the rollback.
- The final `SagaInstance.State` stored in the database is `Compensated`.

***

## saga_id as Cross-Trace Correlation

Because saga steps run in a background poll loop that does not inherit the HTTP request's trace
context, each saga step span is technically a separate root trace in OTLP terms. The `saga.saga_id`
tag set on every step span is the mechanism for correlating them.

In the Aspire Dashboard:

1. Trigger any demo endpoint and note the `sagaId` in the response body.
2. Open **Traces** and use the attribute search or filter bar to search for
   `saga.saga_id = <your-uuid>`.
3. All `saga.step.execute` and `saga.step.compensate` spans for that saga instance appear,
   giving you a complete step-by-step history.

The tag name is `saga.saga_id` and its value is the `SagaInstance.Id` UUID. This tag is set in
`SagaStepExecutor.ProcessEntryAsync` via `activity?.SetTag("saga.saga_id", entry.SagaId.ToString())`.

Note for contributors: connecting saga step spans back to the originating HTTP trace via a stored
`TraceParent` on the `SagaInstance` row — similar to how `OutboxMessage` does it — would allow
the full saga lifecycle to appear as one unified trace tree. This is not currently implemented
and is tracked as future work.

***

## How to Read Outbox Lag

Outbox lag is the time between when an integration event was enqueued (the producer's
`SaveChangesAsync` commit) and when it was actually published to the broker (the
`outbox.publish` span).

To measure lag in the Dashboard:

1. Find the `Mediator.Send` span for a command that produces an integration event (e.g.
   `CreateProductCommand`).
2. Note its **end timestamp** — this is approximately when `SaveChangesAsync` committed and the
   outbox row was written.
3. Find the `outbox.publish` span for the same message (match by `messaging.message_id`, or by
   `messaging.destination` + approximate time).
4. The **start timestamp** of `outbox.publish` minus the end timestamp of the producer span is
   the outbox lag for that message.

Under normal conditions with the default `OutboxPublisherOptions.PollInterval` of 2 seconds and
`BatchSize` of 50, lag is typically 0–4 seconds. Under heavy load, lag grows as the batch fills.
Reduce `PollInterval` or increase `BatchSize` to tune.

The `OutboxPublisherOptions` defaults:

| Setting | Default | Effect |
| ---------------- | --------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `BatchSize` | 50 | Messages processed per poll cycle |
| `PollInterval` | 2 seconds | Sleep between cycles when queue is non-empty |
| `MaxAttempts` | 5 | Publish attempts before transitioning row to `Failed` |
| `RetryBaseDelay` | 1 second | Exponential backoff base delay |

A message in `OutboxStatus.Failed` will not be retried automatically. Monitor for `Failed` rows
in the `outbox_messages` table and alert on them — they represent messages that could not be
delivered after all attempts.

***

## Pitfalls and Common Gaps

### Background services that do not start an activity

`SagaStepExecutor` and `OutboxPublisherBackgroundService` are `BackgroundService` implementations.
Their `ExecuteAsync` loop does not have an ambient `Activity` unless one is explicitly started.
This means:

- Any log message emitted inside the loop but outside a span will have no `TraceId` attached in
  structured logs.
- Any child activity started without an explicit parent context appears as a root span in OTLP.

If you add custom background services to your application and want their spans connected to
a broader trace, you must restore the parent context manually — the same pattern used by
`OutboxPublisherBackgroundService` with `ActivityContext.TryParse`.

### async void timers and fire-and-forget

Avoid `async void` methods and `_ = Task.Run(...)` inside handlers or background services.
Exceptions thrown on `async void` paths crash the process without ending any open spans, leaving
dangling incomplete spans in the Dashboard. Use `async Task` and `await` throughout.

### Gateway observability

The standalone `Kun.Gateway` host registers `AddKunObservability` with service name
`kun-gateway`, configured through `KunObservability`. EF instrumentation is disabled because
this host does not access EF. Native AOT hosts must set `IncludeEfCore=false`; a runtime-feature
guard removes that reflection-based path at link time and rejects attempts to enable it at runtime. ASP.NET request spans cover proxy and JWKS requests, while
HttpClient instrumentation covers downstream calls; there is no separate custom transform span.
The gateway remains in the Native AOT audit. Consumers that reference the gateway package in
their own host choose their own observability registration.

### Key span names to recognize at a glance

| Span name | Source | Meaning |
| ---------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `Mediator.Send {Type}` | `Kun.Mediator` | A command or query was dispatched |
| `outbox.publish` | `Kun.EventBus.Outbox` | An outbox row was published to the broker |
| `grpc.server` | `Kun.Grpc` | A unary or streaming gRPC call was handled |
| `saga.step.execute` | `Kun.Saga` | A saga step ran forward |
| `saga.step.compensate` | `Kun.Saga` | A saga step ran in compensation |

# Command 校验指南（Kun.Validation）

:::info 镜像页
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 [`docs/guides/validating-commands.md`](https://github.com/idadawn/kun/blob/v2026.10.25/docs/guides/validating-commands.md)（`v2026.10.25`）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（[ADR-001 D1.8](/design/adr/adr-001-kun-relationship.md)）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见[与 Qian 的关系](/sdk/kun/with-qian.md)。改动请提到 kun 仓库。
:::

> 怎么在一个 Command/Query Handler 上挂校验，并且让失败以 `Result.Fail(Error.Validation(...))` 而不是异常的形式流到调用方。
>
> 参考：`docs/architecture/ADR-011-Result-async-extensions.md` · `docs/architecture/ADR-014-Validation-Result-behavior.md` · `src/Kun.Validation/AGENTS.md`

## 适用对象

在 `neuroagent-csharp` 或其他下游服务里新加一条 Command/Query，打算：

- 用 `IRequest<Result>` 或 `IRequest<Result<TValue>>` 返回业务结果（而不是抛 `ValidationException` 让 ASP.NET / gRPC 中间件翻译）；
- 在 Handler 之外把"请求形状合法性"（非空、长度、枚举范围等）挡住；
- 写单元测试时能直接断言 `result.Error.Code == "request.invalid"`，不需要 `Assert.ThrowsAsync<ValidationException>`。

如果你只写内部小工具、Handler 返回 `TResponse` 且可以接受异常语义，见下方 `ValidationPipelineBehavior` 路径；否则默认选 Result 路径。

## 选型决策树

Kun.Validation 目前出三个 Pipeline Behavior，按 Handler 响应类型二选一：

| Handler 响应签名 | 选的 Behavior | 失败时的行为 | 注册扩展 |
| ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `IRequest<TResponse>`（非 Result） | `ValidationPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>` | 抛 `ValidationException` | `AddValidationBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>()` |
| `IRequest<Result<TValue>>` | `ValidationResultPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TValue>` | 返回 `Result<TValue>.Fail(Error.Validation("request.invalid", …))` | `AddValidationResultBehavior<TRequest, TValue>()` |
| `IRequest<Result>`（无返回值命令） | `ValidationResultPipelineBehavior<TRequest>` | 返回 `Result.Fail(Error.Validation("request.invalid", …))` | `AddValidationResultBehavior<TRequest>()` |

> **铁律**：同一 `TRequest` 不要同时注册抛出版 + Result 版。Pipeline 会按注册顺序串成链，第二个 Behavior 跑在第一个已经翻译过的结果上，产生双层包装的校验消息。Kun 不在运行时拦截该错配（成本高、场景罕见），只靠 Code Review + 这份文档挡。

## 例 1：`Result<TValue>` 命令

场景：下单命令 `CreateOrderCommand → Result<OrderDto>`，两个校验器（数量 > 0、产品 ID 不为空）。

### Command + Validator

```csharp
public sealed record CreateOrderCommand(Guid ProductId, int Quantity)
    : IRequest<Result<OrderDto>>;

public sealed class CreateOrderQuantityValidator : IValidator<CreateOrderCommand>
{
    public ValueTask<ValidationResult> ValidateAsync(
        CreateOrderCommand instance,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        if (instance.Quantity > 0) return ValueTask.FromResult(ValidationResult.Success);

        return ValueTask.FromResult(ValidationResult.Failure(
        [
            new ValidationError(
                PropertyName: nameof(instance.Quantity),
                Code: "order.quantity.greaterThanZero",
                Message: "Quantity must be greater than 0."),
        ]));
    }
}

public sealed class CreateOrderProductIdValidator : IValidator<CreateOrderCommand>
{
    public ValueTask<ValidationResult> ValidateAsync(
        CreateOrderCommand instance,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        if (instance.ProductId != Guid.Empty) return ValueTask.FromResult(ValidationResult.Success);

        return ValueTask.FromResult(ValidationResult.Failure(
        [
            new ValidationError(
                PropertyName: nameof(instance.ProductId),
                Code: "order.productId.required",
                Message: "ProductId is required."),
        ]));
    }
}
```

错误码遵循 `{aggregate}.{field}.{constraint}`（`src/Kun.Validation/AGENTS.md` §Common Patterns）。

### DI 注册

```csharp
services.AddValidator<CreateOrderCommand, CreateOrderQuantityValidator>();
services.AddValidator<CreateOrderCommand, CreateOrderProductIdValidator>();

services.AddKunMediator(mediator =>
{
    mediator.AddValidationResultBehavior<CreateOrderCommand, OrderDto>();
    // mediator.AddRequestHandler<...>() — 由源生成器自动填
});
```

`AddValidator<,>` 挂在 `IServiceCollection`，`AddValidationResultBehavior<,>` 挂在 `KunMediatorBuilder`——分开是因为 Validator 是按请求类型注册的 transient，Behavior 是 Mediator pipeline 链上的一环。

### Handler

Handler 直接写成功路径；Validator 失败时 Behavior 已经短路，Handler 不会被调到。

```csharp
public sealed class CreateOrderCommandHandler
    : IRequestHandler<CreateOrderCommand, Result<OrderDto>>
{
    public async ValueTask<Result<OrderDto>> Handle(
        CreateOrderCommand request,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    {
        // 走到这里时 Quantity > 0 且 ProductId != Guid.Empty 已成立。
        var product = await _products.GetAsync(request.ProductId, cancellationToken);
        if (product is null)
            return Result<OrderDto>.Fail(Error.NotFound("product.notFound", "Product not found."));

        var order = await _orders.CreateAsync(product, request.Quantity, cancellationToken);
        return Result<OrderDto>.Ok(OrderDto.From(order));
    }
}
```

### 测试

```csharp
[Fact]
public async Task Validator_fails_returns_request_invalid()
{
    var services = new ServiceCollection();
    services.AddValidator<CreateOrderCommand, CreateOrderQuantityValidator>();
    services.AddKunMediator(m =>
    {
        m.AddRequestHandler<CreateOrderCommand, Result<OrderDto>, CreateOrderCommandHandler>();
        m.AddValidationResultBehavior<CreateOrderCommand, OrderDto>();
    });
    var mediator = services.BuildServiceProvider().GetRequiredService<IMediator>();

    var result = await mediator.Send(new CreateOrderCommand(Guid.NewGuid(), 0), CancellationToken.None);

    Assert.True(result.IsFailure);
    Assert.Equal("request.invalid", result.Error.Code);
    Assert.Equal(ErrorType.Validation, result.Error.Type);
    Assert.Contains("greater than 0", result.Error.Message);
}
```

更多断言帮助（`ResultAssertions.ShouldBeFailure(...)` 等）见 `src/Kun.Testing/AGENTS.md`。

## 例 2：`Result` 命令（无返回值）

场景：删除用户命令 `DeleteUserCommand → Result`，一个校验器（`UserId` 非空）。适用于幂等写命令、删除、标记为已读等"跑完了就行、没什么可返回"的业务。

```csharp
public sealed record DeleteUserCommand(Guid UserId) : IRequest<Result>;

public sealed class DeleteUserValidator : IValidator<DeleteUserCommand>
{
    public ValueTask<ValidationResult> ValidateAsync(
        DeleteUserCommand instance,
        CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
    {
        if (instance.UserId != Guid.Empty) return ValueTask.FromResult(ValidationResult.Success);

        return ValueTask.FromResult(ValidationResult.Failure(
        [
            new ValidationError(
                PropertyName: nameof(instance.UserId),
                Code: "user.userId.required",
                Message: "UserId is required."),
        ]));
    }
}

// DI：
services.AddValidator<DeleteUserCommand, DeleteUserValidator>();
services.AddKunMediator(m =>
{
    m.AddValidationResultBehavior<DeleteUserCommand>();  // 注意：只有一个类型参数
});

// Handler：
public sealed class DeleteUserCommandHandler
    : IRequestHandler<DeleteUserCommand, Result>
{
    public async ValueTask<Result> Handle(DeleteUserCommand r, CancellationToken ct)
    {
        var user = await _users.GetAsync(r.UserId, ct);
        if (user is null) return Result.Fail(Error.NotFound("user.notFound", "User not found."));
        await _users.DeleteAsync(user, ct);
        return Result.Ok();
    }
}
```

`AddValidationResultBehavior<TRequest>()`（单参数）闭合在 `IRequest<Result>` 上；`AddValidationResultBehavior<TRequest, TValue>()`（双参数）闭合在 `IRequest<Result<TValue>>` 上。名字一样，只靠类型参数数量区分。

## 反模式

### 1. 同一 `TRequest` 注册两个 Behavior

```csharp
// ❌ 不要这样
m.AddValidationBehavior<CreateOrderCommand, Result<OrderDto>>();          // 抛出版
m.AddValidationResultBehavior<CreateOrderCommand, OrderDto>();            // Result 版
```

Pipeline 会串成链：第一个 Behavior 跑完（抛出）→ 第二个拿不到 `next()` 的返回 → 要么二次抛 `ValidationException`，要么产生双层包装的 `request.invalid` 消息。跑不出来预期结果，IDE 也不会警告。

### 2. 在 `Result`-Handler 里 `throw new ValidationException(...)`

```csharp
// ❌ 不要这样
public async ValueTask<Result<OrderDto>> Handle(...)
{
    if (request.Quantity < 0)
        throw new ValidationException(/* ... */);   // 业务层不该抛校验异常
    // ...
}
```

把校验放进 Validator；Handler 里用 `Result<TValue>.Fail(Error.Validation(...))` 直接返回。`kun/CLAUDE.md` §Architectural constraints："Business failures use `Result` / `Result<T>`, not exceptions." 抛异常会破坏下游 `Match / Bind / Tap` 组合链（ADR-011）。

### 3. 在 Validator 里调数据库 / 外部服务

```csharp
// ❌ 不要这样
public async ValueTask<ValidationResult> ValidateAsync(CreateOrderCommand r, CancellationToken ct)
{
    var product = await _db.Products.FindAsync(r.ProductId, ct);   // 跨层了
    if (product is null) return ValidationResult.Failure(/* ... */);
    // ...
}
```

Validator 只处理"请求形状合法性"（类型、范围、非空、正则）。凡是需要外部状态（"ProductId 对应的产品是否存在"、"该用户是否有权限"）的判断都是语义校验，归 Handler。Validator 纯函数化保证：AOT 友好、单元测试不需要 mock 任何 DbContext、Pipeline 中多个 Validator 可以并行跑。

## 排错

- **Behavior 没生效**：检查 `AddKunMediator(m => …)` 里是否真的调了 `AddValidation…Behavior`；源生成器只注册 Handler 本身，Behavior 需要显式挂到 builder。
- **打了 `AddValidator<,>()` 但 Validator 没跑**：确认 Validator 实现了 `IValidator<T>`（not `IValidator<TRequest, TResponse>`），且 `T` 精确匹配 Command 类型（`CreateOrderCommand` 不是 `object`）。
- **`Result.Error.Message` 为空**：Validator 返回了 `ValidationResult.Failure(errors)`，但 `errors` 数组里每个 `ValidationError.Message` 是空的。Behavior 用 `string.Join("; ", errs.Select(e => e.Message))`，空消息会拼出空字符串。

## 相关

- [ADR-011 Result async extensions](/sdk/kun/architecture/adr-011-result-async-extensions.md)—`Result<T>` 的 `Map/Bind/Tap/Ensure/Match` 组合面。
- [ADR-014 Validation Result behavior](/sdk/kun/architecture/adr-014-validation-result-behavior.md)—两个 Result 版 Behavior 的设计决策。
- [src/Kun.Validation/AGENTS.md](https://github.com/idadawn/kun/blob/v2026.10.25/src/Kun.Validation/AGENTS.md)—Validator 规范、错误码命名模式。

# 审计：同事务实体记录与 PostgreSQL 命令哈希链

:::info 镜像页
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 [`docs/security/audit-log.md`](https://github.com/idadawn/kun/blob/v2026.10.25/docs/security/audit-log.md)（`v2026.10.25`）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（[ADR-001 D1.8](/design/adr/adr-001-kun-relationship.md)）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见[与 Qian 的关系](/sdk/kun/with-qian.md)。改动请提到 kun 仓库。
:::

实体审计入口为 `Kun.Auditing.AddKunAuditing<TContext>()`：在业务 `SavingChanges` 阶段把 `AuditLog` 和 Outbox 行登记到同一个 `KunDbContext`，由同一次保存提交。任一写入失败或业务事务回滚，两类审计记录都回滚；保存失败与取消会撤销暂存行，允许修正业务后重试。

## 实体审计与读取

```csharp
services.AddDbContext<AppDbContext>(options => options.UseNpgsql(connectionString));
services.AddKunDataConventions<AppDbContext>();
services.AddKunAuditing<AppDbContext>();
services.AddAuditable<Order>();
services.AddKunAudit().UseEntityFramework<AppDbContext>();
services.AddKunEventBus(registry => registry.RegisterAuditing());
```

`AddKunAuditing<TContext>()` 与 `AddKunDataConventions<TContext>()` 不登记 `ITenantContext`、`ICurrentUser` 这两个端口，由宿主提供可信实现（`AddKunSecurity()`、`AddKunMultiTenancy()` 等），在数据组件之前或之后登记都生效（见 [When to use ICurrentUser](/sdk/kun/architecture/when-to-use-currentuser.md) 的「端口登记与次序」）。拦截器在上下文创建时按需解析：宿主没有登记 `ICurrentUser` 时按匿名记录；`KunDbContext` 的构造本身需要 `ITenantContext`，单租户宿主显式登记 `NullTenantContext.Instance`。`AddKunAuditing<TContext>()` 在宿主 `OnModelCreating` 前登记 `AuditLog`，使 `KunDbContext` 对它应用租户过滤。多租户宿主仍需装配 `AddKunTenantRls<TContext>()` 和数据库 RLS 策略。

- 每个被 `AddAuditable<TEntity>()` 声明的实体变更生成一行 `audit_logs` 与一行 Outbox，二者共享 Guid v7 标识。
- `kun.audit.event.v2` 使用字符串 `tenantId` / `userId`，从上下文填写；`AuditContext` 可覆盖 actor、来源 IP 与 trace，`ActorType` 支持 `user/service/agent/system`。
- 实体需要客户端已知的主键（推荐下面的 Guid v7 约定）；服务端自增键不能在 `SavingChanges` 阶段获得最终值。
- 不自动采集实体内容，避免把敏感字段写进审计载荷。实体审计写入失败会使业务保存失败；旧 `SwallowWriterExceptions` 选项不控制此入口。
- `IAuditReader.QueryAsync` 在数据库内按当前租户、主体、动作、资源与时间过滤，按时间、ID 倒序，限制每次 1–1,000 条。查询租户必须与当前上下文一致，不支持通过查询参数越权切换租户。

## 数据约定

模型配置最后调用 `modelBuilder.ApplyKunDataConventions()`，保存拦截器通过 `AddKunDataConventions<TContext>()` 自动装配：

- 表、列、键、索引使用 snake_case；未赋值的 Guid 主键生成 v7，显式主键保持不变。
- `IAuditedObject` 新增时写 `created_at/created_by`，修改时仅刷新 `updated_at/updated_by`，禁止改写创建字段。
- 主体支持 `string`、`Guid?`、`long?`、`int?`。匿名或系统操作写 null，不用空 Guid 或 0 冒充主体；无法转换的已认证主体拒绝保存。
- 主体取自上下文创建时解析到的 `ICurrentUser`；宿主没有登记身份适配器时按匿名写 null。数据约定不登记 `ICurrentUser`，身份适配器与它的登记先后不影响结果。
- C# 无约束泛型的 `T?` 不会把值类型自动变成可空值类型。已有 `AggregateRoot<TKey>`（Guid 主体）需显式迁移为 `AggregateRoot<TKey, Guid?>`，并生成相应数据库迁移；旧公共基类保持兼容。
- 审计实体映射 shadow `KunRowVersion` 至 PostgreSQL `xmin`。冲突保留 `DbUpdateConcurrencyException`；需要 Result 边界时调用 `SaveChangesResultAsync()`，映射为 `data.concurrency_conflict` / `Conflict`，不自动覆盖获胜写入。

## 命令审计哈希链

```csharp
// NpgsqlDataSource 由宿主管理生命周期。
services.AddKunAudit(options => options.DefaultActorType = AuditActorType.Agent)
    .UsePostgresChain(dataSource, "audit");
services.AddKunMediator(builder => builder.AddAuditBehavior<CreateOrder, Result<Guid>>());
```

部署迁移阶段显式调用 `PostgresAuditChain.EnsureCreatedAsync()`；正常追加不建表。PostgreSQL 需 15+（测试为 16），使用 `UNIQUE NULLS NOT DISTINCT` 拦截相同前序，包括首条 null 前序。

`PostgresAuditChain` 同时实现 `IAuditChainState` 和 `IAuditSink`，必须使用同一个实例。每次追加在事务内创建或锁定该租户唯一链头（`FOR UPDATE`），读取最新 tip、插入记录并推进 tip 后提交。采用 READ COMMITTED 的语句快照，避免持续写入副本使等待方拿着旧的 SERIALIZABLE 快照反复重试；租户行锁提供完整的读改写串行化。`content_hash`、`(tenant_key, seq)` 和 `(tenant_key, prev_hash)` 唯一约束防止分叉。全局链与任意租户字符串使用不同键空间。

`WriteAsync()` 只接受当前追加作用域里租户、前序和内容哈希都匹配的一条记录；回调失败时记录与链头一起回滚。回调可能因数据库瞬时冲突重试，因此不得夹带事务外副作用。

`AuditEntry.ActorType` 默认 `unknown`，保持历史条目的哈希兼容；明确主体类型的新条目采用固定字段顺序的 JSON 编码后计算 SHA-256，避免分隔符歧义。用 `AuditContentHasher.Compute(entry)` 重放；变更 actor 类型也会改变哈希。数据库额外保存 UTC ticks，避免 PostgreSQL 微秒精度损失。

```csharp
string? previous = null;
await foreach (var row in chain.ReadAsync(tenantId, cancellationToken))
{
    if (row.PrevHash != previous || AuditContentHasher.Compute(row) != row.ContentHash)
        throw new InvalidOperationException("审计链断裂");
    previous = row.ContentHash;
}
```

读取哈希链是基础设施 API，调用方必须先授权。命令 Pipeline 延续既有行为：审计失败记录告警，不覆盖 handler 的返回值或原始异常。它不承诺与业务事务原子提交；需要业务与审计原子性的实体记录使用前述 `AddKunAuditing<TContext>()`。

## 旧入口迁移

- `Kun.Audit.EntityFrameworkCore.AuditSaveChangesInterceptor` 与 `AddKunAuditEntityFrameworkCore()` 是业务保存后再写审计的旧路径，已标记 `KUNAUDIT001` 废弃警告。
- `UseEventBus()`、`EventBusAuditWriter` 与 `kun.audit.record.v1` 路径已废弃；迁移到 `AddKunAuditing<TContext>()`，不要同时挂两个实体审计拦截器。
- 无泛型 `AddKunAuditing()` 与 `AddAuditingInterceptor()` 保留兼容旧 `kun.audit.event.v1`，新宿主采用泛型入口；v1 的 Guid 载荷不能承载任意字符串主体，不能把类型改动伪装为原 v1 事件。
- `RegisterAuditing()` 同时注册 v1/v2 稳定 ID，同时登记源生成的 JSON 类型信息；消费方应先同时支持两版，再切生产者，待历史消息排空后移除旧订阅。

## 验证

`TransactionalAuditTests` 验证业务／审计／Outbox 同提交与回滚、审计写入失败、失败后重试、创建字段保持、空主体、xmin 冲突与租户读取；`PostgresAuditChainTests` 用两个独立数据源并发追加 1,000 条，逐条重放验证无分叉，并覆盖追加后故障回滚及全局／租户隔离。

# Multi-Tenancy: Row-Level Security as Defence in Depth

:::info 镜像页
本页镜像自 kun 仓库 [`docs/security/multi-tenancy-rls.md`](https://github.com/idadawn/kun/blob/v2026.10.25/docs/security/multi-tenancy-rls.md)（`v2026.10.25`）。Kun 文档与代码不一致处以代码为准（[ADR-001 D1.8](/design/adr/adr-001-kun-relationship.md)）；Qian 对 Kun 的选用与约束见[与 Qian 的关系](/sdk/kun/with-qian.md)。改动请提到 kun 仓库。
:::

Kun enforces tenant isolation at two independent layers:

1. **Application layer** — `KunDbContext` applies a global query filter to every
   entity implementing `IMultiTenant`, scoping reads by `ITenantContext.TenantId`.
   This is implemented inside the EF Core query pipeline.
2. **Database layer** — PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) policies defined on
   each tenant-scoped table, driven by the session variable
   `app.current_tenant_id` that Kun pushes in on every connection open.

Either layer alone is enough for the happy path; both together give a
belt-and-braces posture: a bug in the ORM filter does not silently leak rows,
and a bug in the RLS policy is caught by the ORM filter. This document covers
the second layer.

***

## 查询过滤器与共享模型

`KunDbContext` 的租户过滤器通过当前执行查询的 DbContext 读取租户，不把第一个宿主的 `ITenantContext` 实例留在缓存模型里。这样同租户的多个宿主或请求访问器复用模型时，旧访问器退出作用域或切到其它租户都不会改变新请求的过滤条件。

不继承 `KunDbContext` 的上下文须实现 `IKunMultiTenantDbContext`，并在 `OnModelCreating` 中调用 `modelBuilder.ApplyKunMultiTenantFilters(this)`。**迁移要求**：原 `ITenantContext` 重载标记 KUNTENANT001，保留方法签名但在模型构建时明确抛出异常，不能继续装载不安全过滤器。只捕获租户 ID 常量也无法兼容默认共享模型，因此旧调用者必须改为当前 DbContext 入口。继续使用 `AddKunTenantRls<TContext>()` 的双拦截器与模型缓存装配；模型缓存不能替代数据库隔离。

`TenantContextBindingTests` 使用 PostgreSQL 和受限应用角色单独验证 EF 过滤层，明确复用同一个模型，并让前一个访问器退出作用域或切到另一个租户；基础类与 DbContext 重载在默认和按租户缓存两种配置下都须只返回当前请求的租户行。旧入口的明确拒绝另有回归。

## The TenantRlsConnectionInterceptor

`src/Kun.EntityFrameworkCore/Interceptors/TenantRlsConnectionInterceptor.cs`

The interceptor hooks EF Core's `DbConnectionInterceptor` events:

- `ConnectionOpenedAsync` → emits `SET app.current_tenant_id = '<tenant>'`
  when `ITenantContext.TenantId` is non-empty; `RESET app.current_tenant_id`
  otherwise.
- `ConnectionClosingAsync` → emits `RESET app.current_tenant_id` so pooled
  connections never leak the previous request's tenant scope.

Only activates when the underlying `DbConnection` is `Npgsql.NpgsqlConnection`
(namespace-prefix check on the type's FQN). Other providers are silently
no-ops so this module does not need to take a direct Npgsql dependency.

### SQL-injection guard

`SET` statements cannot be parameterised, so the tenant id is inlined into the
command text. The interceptor refuses to emit the command unless the value
matches the strict whitelist:

```
^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$
```

Exposed as `TenantRlsConnectionInterceptor.SafeTenantIdPattern`. A tenant id
that does not match (spaces, quotes, semicolons, etc.) throws
`InvalidOperationException` rather than being silently coerced.

### Registration and wiring

`AddKunEntityFrameworkCore` registers the interceptor as Scoped. It does not
activate until the caller wires it into a specific `DbContextOptionsBuilder`:

```csharp
services.AddKunEntityFrameworkCore();
services.AddDbContext<CatalogDbContext>((sp, opts) =>
{
    opts.UseNpgsql(connectionString);
    opts.AddInterceptors(sp.GetRequiredService<TenantRlsConnectionInterceptor>());
});
```

Per-scope semantics: each resolved `CatalogDbContext` picks up the scope's
`ITenantContext`, so each request gets the tenant id scoped to itself.

***

## Database-side policy template

The interceptor only sets the session variable — it does not create RLS
policies. Those live with the service's schema migrations. Template for a
tenant-scoped table `orders`:

```sql
ALTER TABLE orders ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
-- FORCE is critical: without it the table owner (the account running
-- migrations) bypasses RLS and all queries from the service would ignore
-- the policy. FORCE makes the policy apply even to the owner.
ALTER TABLE orders FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

CREATE POLICY orders_tenant_scope ON orders
    USING      (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true))
    WITH CHECK (tenant_id = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true));
```

- `USING` — rows visible to `SELECT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE` operations.
- `WITH CHECK` — rows permitted by `INSERT`/`UPDATE` operations.

Without `WITH CHECK`, a user could insert a row belonging to another tenant,
then lose sight of it via `USING`.

The `true` second argument to `current_setting` is _missing_ok_ — PostgreSQL
returns an empty string instead of raising if the variable is unset. Pair with
a `NOT NULL` constraint on `tenant_id` so the empty-string case does not match
real rows.

***

## Tests

`tests/Kun.IntegrationTests/MultiTenancy/TenantRlsTests.cs` spins a Postgres 16
container via Testcontainers and verifies:

- **RLS isolates rows without the EF filter**: the test entity deliberately
  does _not_ implement `IMultiTenant`, so EF's global query filter cannot
  account for the observed tenant isolation — any separation comes entirely
  from the RLS policy driven by the interceptor.
- **Cross-tenant writes are rejected**: inserting a row with another tenant's
  id surfaces a `DbUpdateException` (Postgres code `42501 / 23514`).
- **Unsafe tenant ids are blocked before hitting the server**: a tenant id
  containing `'; DROP TABLE ...; --` trips the whitelist and throws
  `InvalidOperationException`.

***

## Operational notes

- **Connection pooling**: the `ConnectionClosingAsync` RESET ensures a pooled
  connection returned to Npgsql does not carry the previous request's tenant
  scope into the next borrower. A failure to RESET is logged (warning) rather
  than thrown, because the connection is about to close anyway and we do not
  want to convert a close-path hiccup into a user-visible error.
- **Providers other than PostgreSQL**: the interceptor is a no-op. MySQL's
  user-defined variables use different syntax (`SET @...`) and MySQL does not
  have first-class RLS; if you need equivalent enforcement there, layer a
  session-level procedure or a column-level check constraint.
- **Non-tenant-scoped connections**: when a request has no tenant context
  (e.g. an admin console running under `NullTenantContext`), the interceptor
  emits `RESET` so the session variable is cleared. Any RLS policy evaluating
  against `current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true)` will then match
  only rows whose `tenant_id` equals the empty string — typically nothing.

## 后台链路与生产装配（S1-KUN-001）

```csharp
services.AddKunSecurity();
services.AddKunMultiTenancy(options => options.Production = true);
services.AddDbContext<AppDbContext>(options => options.UseNpgsql(connectionString));
services.AddKunTenantRls<AppDbContext>();

app.UseAuthentication();
app.UseKunMultiTenancy();
```

`AppDbContext` 继承 `KunDbContext`，或实现 `IKunMultiTenantDbContext`。泛型 RLS 入口自动附加两种拦截器与缓存键；无泛型旧重载只注册拦截器，保留既有手动装配的兼容性。生产 HTTP 链路只读取已认证身份的唯一 `tenant_id`，值需满足 1–128 个 ASCII 字母、数字、点、下划线或连字符；无令牌、非法令牌、缺失或非法租户均返回 401，不回退请求头或 `default`。匿名端点应显式放在租户中间件之外。

`AddKunSecurity` 和 `AddKunMultiTenancy` 无论先后注册，`ITenantContext` 都解析为同一 `AsyncLocalTenantContext` 单例。原 `JwtTenantContext` 仍保留公共类型以兼容既有代码，但 DI 只把它作为 `ITenantIdSource` 注册；显式作用域覆盖 HTTP 来源，显式空作用域会屏蔽 HTTP 来源。第三方旧 `ITenantContext` 实现仍可编译；需要后台回灌时须实现 `BeginScope`，默认接口方法会明确拒绝不支持的操作。

消费端在解析 handler 及其 scoped 依赖前，从信封恢复 `MessageContext.TenantId` 并打开作用域；多租户宿主的缺失或非法租户消息在幂等标记前进入死信队列。租户标识是内部可信发布者的信封元数据，不应直接接收外部请求字段；消息代理权限仍需由宿主限制。Outbox 发布器逐条恢复租户，Saga 执行器对每条队列记录创建独立 DI scope，执行与补偿均以 `SagaInstance.TenantId` 打开租户作用域，异常后也会释放。

在自定义后台任务中用 `using (tenantContext.BeginScope(tenantId))` 包围处理逻辑；不要把某个租户的 DbContext 保存为单例。PgBouncer 事务池下仍需显式事务，自动装配不改变其事务边界要求。

验收证据位于 `BackgroundTenantFlowTests`（真实 PG + RabbitMQ，A/B 交替、EF 与 RLS 独立断言、无租户／非法租户死信）、`ProductionTenantTests`（真实 RSA JWT 验证）、`TenantContextRegistrationTests`、`SagaTenantScopeTests` 与 `OutboxPublisherBackgroundServiceTests`。
